headline: State Week: A dark cloud looming for Illinois' finances
summary: This week's State Week discusses the new state forecast of a shortfall of up to $2.4 billion next fiscal year, tied to federal policy changes. The show notes do not mention higher education or community colleges.

headline: Illinois House to vote on bill allowing striking workers to receive unemployment benefits
summary: The Illinois House is expected to vote on a bill that would let striking workers collect unemployment insurance once a strike lasts more than two weeks; the description matches HB2565. The report lays out the arguments of supporters and of manufacturing and retail groups over cost and strike length, and notes the bill would go to the Senate in January if it passes the House.

headline: New Rule Changes the Future of Programmatic Accreditation
summary: A new U.S. Department of Education rule requires programmatic accreditors to show they are independent of related professional trade groups in funding, staffing, office space and volunteer decision-making, starting in July. The article weighs whether the change addresses concerns about trade-group influence over program accreditation.

headline: HB2565: Added Co-Sponsor (after Nov. 17 return to House 2nd Reading calendar)
summary: The bill, which would change how the Unemployment Insurance Act treats workers in a labor dispute, moved again during veto session. On Nov. 17 the House Rules Committee approved it for consideration, returned it to the 2nd Reading calendar and recommended adopting House Floor Amendment No. 2, so it is now eligible for a House floor vote; a co-sponsor was added Nov. 20.

headline: HB5236: Added as Alternate Co-Sponsor (Senate)
summary: The Digital Library Protection Act passed the House 99-0-1 in April and is pending in the Senate Assignments Committee. It picked up additional Senate alternate co-sponsors on Nov. 6, Nov. 17 and Nov. 19 but has not yet been assigned to a Senate committee.

headline: Senate appropriations committee proposes $15B in additional Pell Grant funding
summary: The Senate Appropriations Committee's fiscal 2027 Labor-HHS-Education bill would put an extra $15 billion toward the Pell Grant program to cover a shortfall the Congressional Budget Office projects at about $16.9 billion. The maximum award would stay at $7,395 for 2027-28. The bill would also raise Education Department discretionary funding to $93.9 billion and hold Federal Work-Study, FSEOG, the Office for Civil Rights and the Institute of Education Sciences at current levels, with a Dec. 11 funding deadline still ahead.

headline: Voicing opposition to EDGAR changes
summary: The Education Department has proposed changes to its general grant regulations (EDGAR) that community colleges say would let the agency end grants early and attach new conditions to funding. Congress has blocked a parallel government-wide OMB grant rule through Dec. 11, and college advocates told a congressional briefing they want that block extended and the EDGAR changes stopped too.

headline: Taxing AI: Alternative Approaches
summary: This Congressional Research Service report (R49520) looks at proposals in the 119th Congress to tax artificial intelligence. It covers the arguments for, such as labor-market disruption and lost wage-tax revenue, and the arguments against, such as productivity and competitiveness. It reviews possible tools, including per-unit or value-based excise taxes on AI tokens, compute and chip taxes, gross receipts taxes and changes to income-tax rules, and it discusses the token tax proposed in H.R. 10044.

headline: Unemployment for workers on strike gains support following donations
summary: Reports that HB2565, which would extend unemployment benefits to striking workers, had a second amendment cleared by House Rules and gained House co-sponsors ahead of a possible veto-session floor vote. It cites a state fiscal note estimating a cost to the unemployment trust fund of $0.7 million to $1 million a year, an estimate business groups dispute, and notes the House returns Dec. 1.

headline: Durbin Reintroduces Legislation To Protect Student Loan Borrowers
summary: The release announces the reintroduction in the Senate of the Student Loan Borrower Bill of Rights. The bill would set uniform servicing and disclosure rules for federal and private student loans, standardize how payments are applied across loans, and let borrowers take servicers to court rather than arbitration.

headline: It's just a bill
summary: Capitol Fax's daily bills roundup notes that HB2565, the striking-workers unemployment bill, moved to second reading in the House on Nov. 17. It summarizes objections from employer groups, including the Illinois Manufacturers' Association, about the bill's effect on the unemployment insurance trust fund.

headline: Senate GOP Proposes Steady Education Funding, Setting Up Budget Showdown
summary: Senate Republican appropriators released a fiscal 2027 Labor-HHS-Education bill that keeps most federal education programs at about current levels. That sets up negotiations with a House version that cuts more. The bill adds language requiring TRIO programs to be run in line with past practice and congressional intent, after this year's TRIO competitions drew bipartisan concern, and it gives Perkins career-technical education grants a small increase. Funding is frozen under a stopgap that runs through Dec. 11.

headline: Prairie State students call for changes to Pioneer Book Bundle
summary: At Prairie State College's Oct. 27 board meeting, the student trustee presented survey results on the college's automatic course-materials bundle, with students reporting trouble opting out and paying for materials some courses don't use. Administrators said ending the bundle would raise costs but they are open to changes. The board also approved a tentative 2026 property tax levy, with final levy action expected in December.

headline: Post-Midterm Elections: State of Play in Education
summary: This policy-firm alert expects little work in the lame-duck session and more short-term funding extensions after the Dec. 11 deadline. It says the larger appropriations decisions will likely wait for the Democratic-led Congress next year. It identifies Pell Grants, where a projected $17 billion FY2027 shortfall competes with calls for a larger maximum award, and the 2025 federal loan limits as likely higher-education fights, with veto power and the Senate's 60-vote threshold limiting what can pass.

headline: Washington Watch: Senate Republicans release education funding bill
summary: Senate Republicans' FY2027 Labor-HHS-Education spending bill would add more than $15 billion to cover the projected Pell Grant shortfall but keep the maximum award flat, unlike the House version. TRIO and Perkins CTE get modest increases, Strengthening Community Colleges Training Grants rise by $5 million, and WIOA formula grants and campus-based aid stay level. The current continuing resolution runs out Dec. 11, and another stopgap is expected.

headline: Priorities and Prospects for AI Legislation in the New Congress
summary: This law-firm client alert looks at the federal AI bills likely to come up when Democrats take control of the 120th Congress. It lists data centers, frontier-model safety, cybersecurity, worker protections, civil rights and national security, and says divided government leaves the scope and timing of any law uncertain. It also notes that a data center bill advanced in the Senate on Nov. 9 and that AI chip export provisions could be attached to the defense authorization bill during the lame-duck session.

headline: Senate Appropriations Committee Releases Final Five FY 2027 Funding Bills
summary: The Senate Appropriations Committee released bill text, an explanatory statement and a summary for its fiscal 2027 Labor, Health and Human Services, Education, and Related Agencies bill, one of five spending bills released that day. The release describes the bill's education spending only in general terms. Program-level figures are in the linked bill documents.

headline: Illinois' projected $927M surplus could give way to $2.4B deficit next year amid federal changes
summary: The state budget office projects a surplus in fiscal 2027 but a gap of nearly $2.4 billion in fiscal 2028 as federal Medicaid and food-aid changes take effect. Education groups are already lining up funding requests, including the Illinois Federation of Teachers' push for more K-12 money and a University of Illinois request; community colleges are not discussed. The outlook frames the budget climate for any community college funding ramp in 2027.

headline: GOMB Releases Annual Economic and Fiscal Policy Report
outlet: Governor's Office of Management and Budget (State of Illinois Newsroom)
summary: The state budget office's annual report projects a small fiscal 2027 surplus after proposed set-asides and a roughly $2.4 billion gap for fiscal 2028, driven by spending growth and federal cuts to food assistance and health care. The release does not address higher education; the full report is linked from the release.

headline: With new Democratic Congress incoming, Pritzker calls for federal AI regulations
summary: Gov. JB Pritzker called for federal regulation of artificial intelligence as a Democratic-controlled Congress prepares to take office in January. The article is paywalled and could not be read, so this summary rests on the headline alone.

headline: Aurora mayoral recall referendum passes, Joliet data center question fails
summary: An election-night roundup of suburban ballot questions reports that voters approved Moraine Valley Community College's $115 million bond issue. The report says the money will expand training in fields such as emergency medical services and auto repair.

headline: City Colleges, Faculty and Professional Staff Reach Tentative Contract Hours Before Strike Set to Begin
summary: Local 1600 and City Colleges reached a tentative four-year agreement overnight, calling off the strike planned for Monday. The union says it includes raises that keep up with the cost of living, protected health insurance and AI safeguards; it goes to a member ratification vote and then to the City Colleges board.

headline: City Colleges of Chicago reach late-night tentative contract agreement to avoid strike
summary: The Sun-Times reports the overnight tentative agreement between Local 1600 and City Colleges, citing the union's description of a four-year deal with inflation-matching salaries, protected health insurance, AI safeguards and a path toward free developmental education. Classes continued as scheduled while the deal awaits ratification and board approval.

headline: Malcolm X College West Campus reopens with Danny K. Davis Community Center
summary: Malcolm X College reopened its expanded West Campus on Madison Street after a renovation that City Colleges puts at $20 million. The building's former West Side Learning Center is now the Danny K. Davis Community Center; Chancellor Juan Salgado and Mayor Brandon Johnson attended the ribbon cutting.

headline: Faculty and staff at City Colleges of Chicago vote 96 percent to strike; walkout set for October 19
summary: An advocacy site's account of the City Colleges strike vote and the bargaining issues, written from a socialist viewpoint that is critical of union leadership. It also says Prairie State College faculty had been working without a contract since August, following staff layoffs.

headline: City Colleges Staff Announce Oct. 19 Strike Date as Contract Negotiations Continue
summary: Local 1600 set an Oct. 19 strike date at City Colleges after 96% of voting members backed a work stoppage. The union had been bargaining since February, before the faculty and professional contracts expired in mid-July, and sought better wages, smaller classes, AI protections, affordable health insurance and free developmental education.

headline: Mark R. Stephens Resigns as Chair of Triton College Board of Trustees
summary: Triton College announced that Mark R. Stephens stepped down as chair of its Board of Trustees on Sept. 4, 2026. He remains a trustee.

headline: PSC reports near $8 million deficit as enrollment plummets
summary: Prairie State College ended fiscal 2026 with a deficit of about $3.35 million in its two main operating funds and projects a shortfall near $8 million for 2026-27. Officials point to enrollment that has fallen by half since 2012 and late Cook County property tax payments, and have made spending cuts under an action plan.

headline: SSC board passes tentative 2027 budget
summary: South Suburban College's board approved a tentative fiscal 2027 budget projecting a surplus of about $89,000, its seventh straight balanced budget, covering higher health insurance costs and new positions. Trustees also disagreed over creating an honorary, non-voting trustee emeritus seat.
